entry.title: Daily Briefing: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
# Agent N's Hermes News — 24 September 2026

Executive Summary

The week's headline is the coordinated launch of Bot Screen for Hermes Desktop: live streaming of any bot's screen or session, with interactive visual passthrough to the agent's machine. It pulled the community's biggest engagement by far (204 likes, 20k views) and drew the kind of "Finallllly!" reaction reserved for long-requested features. Under the hood, Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21) shipped a --format stream-json flag emitting structured JSONL — the enabling piece for the new Hermes-Claude subscription plugin, which drives the unmodified official Claude CLI while keeping your credentials entirely with the official Claude Code CLI. Around that core: @rlaope open-sourced jeval and shipped OMH+ updates to oh-my-hermes, AgentProto v0.20.0 landed with Hermes among 14 supported integrations, and official channels shared practical guidance from iMessage usage to bug-report etiquette.

Releases

Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21, 21 September 2026)

  • New --format stream-json CLI flag emits structured JSONL for machine-readable output — unlocking scripted and programmatic Hermes Agent workflows and underpinning the Claude plugin pipeline.
  • The release rollup also brings skills auto-load and MCP discovery concurrency improvements.

Bot Screen for Hermes Desktop

  • Streams any bot's screen or session live, adding interactive visual passthrough to the agent's machine — "you can now watch your agents work live."
  • Announced officially by @NousResearch with a launch post from @Teknium on interactive passthrough; @tonbistudio published a walkthrough with a docs link (also amplified by Teknium), giving newcomers an immediate on-ramp.

Ecosystem releases

  • AgentProto v0.20.0 (22 September 2026): a new open-source TypeScript agent runtime listing Hermes among 14 supported integrations — a notable interoperability signal for the agent ecosystem.
  • Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 (18 September 2026): MCP security hardening with per-invocation session scoping plus vector-store changes — adjacent reading for anyone tracking agent tooling trends.

Community

Bot Screen reception. Sentiment was emphatically positive — "Finallllly!", "Much needed!", plus short-but-warm endorsements ("Impressive!", "This is the way") and celebratory replies. This was one of the most-requested Hermes capabilities to date.

Third-party tooling matures — a big week for @rlaope.

  • Open-sourced jeval, a tool for evaluating and visually extracting Jev results.
  • Shipped OMH+ updates to oh-my-hermes adding Jev skills, plugins and aliases, model routing, and JEV-powered workflows — positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for AI-native Hermes Agent users.

Responsive official support. @Teknium shipped a quick fix in response to user feedback, set clear bug-report etiquette in a cache dispute (a reproducible path filed as an issue, or it didn't happen), and clarified provenance in a multi-party thread: the discussed artifact was built by the Nous/Hermes team, not Anthropic.

Curated out: duplicate jeval/OMH link drops, emoji-only replies, engagement bait, and one off-topic Opus 5.5 vs Claude Code take outside Hermes scope.

Tips & Tutorials

  • Run Claude on your existing subscription — without exposing credentials. The Hermes-Claude subscription plugin drives the unmodified official Claude CLI over native stream-json. Its documented auth model keeps credentials entirely with the official Claude Code CLI, so you never hand Hermes an API key. Full details in the deep dive: "Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin."
  • Script your agent. With v0.21.4, pass --format stream-json to get structured JSONL output you can pipe into scripts and programmatic workflows.
  • Watch your agents work. Follow @tonbistudio's Bot Screen walkthrough (docs linked in the post) for the fastest path to live desktop passthrough in Hermes Desktop.
  • Hermes over iMessage. Per @NousResearch, Hermes works over iMessage with any model of your choosing.
  • File better bugs. Reproducible path or it didn't happen: open an issue with clear repro steps first — and expect a fix (Teknium's quick turnaround this week shows it works).

entry.title: Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin
entry.summary: Explains the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin pipeline: Hermes drives the unmodified official claude CLI, communicating via native stream-json, while Hermes retains its own loop, tools, approvals and compaction. Every request spawns a fresh claude process in a private temp directory with native tools/skills disabled so Hermes' tool inventory is what the model sees. An admission relay forwards exactly one upstream request per turn, rejecting native retry attempts locally. Requires Hermes 0.21.4+ and Claude Code CLI (native 2.1.263 qualified); older Hermes versions refuse the plugin cleanly.

entry.title: Hermes Agent Stream JSON Output: New in v0.21.4
entry.summary: Documents Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21), released 21 September 2026, adding a --format stream-json CLI flag that emits structured JSONL (one JSON object per line) instead of plain text, enabling reliable parsing in scripts and pipelines. Update paths include hermes update for git installs, the installer one-liner, or the nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.9.21 Docker image. The same release rolls up roughly 1,812 merged PRs including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency.

entry.title: Hermes-Claude Auth: How Login Works (No API Key)
entry.summary: Details the authentication model of the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: credentials remain entirely with the official Claude Code CLI via claude auth login; the plugin never opens, copies, refreshes or prints credential files, and no API key exists anywhere in the flow. The plugin actively rejects inherited API-key, custom-endpoint and cloud override environment variables, naming conflicting variables without exposing values. Status checks are local (claude auth status reads the local credential store in roughly 0.3s), and separated setups can use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR for dedicated CLI-managed config.

entry.title: AgentProto Review: New Open Agent Runtime (2026)
entry.summary: Review of AgentProto, an open-source TypeScript agentic runtime released 22 September 2026 (v0.20.0) that provides a single interface to start, message, watch and stop coding agents, with quality gates before work lands. Integrates 14 agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, opencode and Mastra. Apache-2.0 licensed with cost limited to model usage. Caveats: single-digit GitHub stars, self-described Tier 2 alpha scaffolding; verdict is early-adopters-only.

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: What Changed
entry.summary: Covers Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0, tagged on GitHub 18 September 2026. Key changes center on MCP security: sessions scoped per invocation with requests authenticated against invocation identity, origin and ownership. Skill archives become ZIP-only with digest verification; ambiguous MCP configuration matches are rejected. Adds vector-store connectors for MongoDB, Azure DocumentDB and Azure Cosmos DB plus in-memory and portable filters. Notes a breaking change with deprecation of the MCP sampling callback.
